audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 and Level 3 read Cho'Gath in both layers while whys[1] says 'You favour level 2' and whys[2] says 'Level 3 flattens to skill'. The packet levelChart and the already-audited mirror both read Skill / Zaahen / Skill / Skill / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath.
audit.why: The mirror has already fixed its side to that chart, so leaving these two rows would put the two directions in direct contradiction — and mirror-fix.js would overwrite them anyway.
audit.corrected: Level 2 flipped to Zaahen and Level 3 to Skill as matched full+content pairs, with ratings set to the inverse of the mirror's (5,6,5,5,5,4,4).

audit.why: The spike story is already right: level 2 edge, level 6 reset on Feast, first item where stacked Feast HP absorbs the burst, two items where he out-tanks. Feast is 80/70/60s and the 60s at rank 3 is now stated so the player can count it.
audit.corrected: Feast's 60s added to breakdown.cooldowns; no spike restructuring needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (1) The page tells the player to build MR for Feast — tldr 'Build MR', winCon 'Build MR', report[0]/report[1], and dosFull[1].t 'Build MR for his R'. Feast is TRUE damage and percent-health; magic resist does nothing against it. The missing-interactions file flags exactly this (resistances-invalidated). (2) Rupture is described only as a knock-up telegraph — it also GROUNDS, which turns off Zaahen's E dash, the one tool he has for leaving a trade.
audit.why: Buying MR to survive an ultimate that ignores resistances is the worst kind of wrong: it costs gold, it feels like preparation, and the player still dies at the same health. And a player who dashes into the crater to answer the knock-up finds he cannot dash back out.
audit.corrected: MR re-pointed at Feral Scream (magic damage) and away from Feast in tldr and dosFull[0].d/[1].t; the grounding on Rupture written into report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's own defect line: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. sequencingCues is 0. Nothing on the page told the player to wait for anything specific before doing anything specific.
audit.why: Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s and it silences — that is the ability that deletes Zaahen, because silence into Feast is the kill. Rupture is a 6s cooldown, so it is never the thing to wait out; the silence is.
audit.corrected: 'Bait Feral Scream before you E in' written into breakdown.cooldowns and mid with the 10s number, plus Rupture's 6s and Feast's 60s.

edits.before: Build MR — dodge his Q, burst his immobile body. Zaahen wins the Feast cooldown windows.
edits.after: MR stops his scream, not Feast — dodge his Q and burst him. Zaahen wins the Feast windows.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Feast: matchup-defining — True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Cho'Gath Feral Scream (10s at rank 3): wait for the silence before you E in. - Rupture (6s): it grounds as well as knocks up. - Feast (60s at rank 3): true damage, so MR does not answer it.

edits.before: Track Cho'Gath's Feast: True-damage execute. Don’t sit low. When it is down — Combo + R him.
edits.after: Rupture grounds as well as knocking up — your E cannot dash out of the crater, so bait it first.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 you hold a real trading edge with E Golden Onslaught engage plus Q, but the moment he hits 6 and R Feast comes online the lane resets to even and skill-dependent — one silenced combo can execute you.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 you hold a real trading edge, but sequence it: Feral Scream is 10s and Rupture grounds you, so bait both before you E in. At 6 Feast resets the lane to even — one silenced combo can execute you.
